en: The Mahāyāna-alaṃkāra-ratnarāja-sūtra, Scroll One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master,
the Imperially Ennobled Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Tianxi’ai at the Guhāvana Monastery in the Kingdom of Jalandhara, Central India, in accordance with imperial decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as a multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
whose names were Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva-mahāsattva and Jñānadarśana Bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrasena, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Guhyagarbha,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryagarbha.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Acalā, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnapāṇi,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Satyasaṃdarśana.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahā-vīrya,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Vajrapāṇi, Sāgaramati, Dharmadhara, and others—
eighty koṭis of Bodhisattvas— all came together for this assembly.
At that time, there were also thirty-two assemblies of devaputras who all gathered together,
with Maheśvara and Nārāyaṇa as their leaders.
Śakra, the King of Devas; Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World;
Sūryadeva, Candradeva, Vāyudeva, and Varuṇadeva—all such hosts of devas gathered there in assembly.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of nāga kings,
namely: the nāga king Apalāla, the nāga king Elapatra,
the nāga king Timiṅgila, and the nāga king Pṛthivīpati.
The nāga king Śataśīrṣa, the nāga king Vyāghra-rūpa-nanda,
the nāga king Takṣaka, the nāga king Gośīrṣa,
the nāga king Mṛgaśīrṣa, and the nāga king Nanda.
The Nāga King Upananda, the Nāga King Matsyaka,
the Nāga King Anavatapta, and the Nāga King Sagarin—
all such nāga kings as these assembled there.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of gandharva kings,
namely: the gandharva king Drumasvara, the gandharva king Susvara,
the gandharva king Sahasrabhuja, and the gandharva king Devendra.
The Gandharva King Joyful Body, the Gandharva King Various Musical Sounds,
the Gandharva King Adorned, and the Gandharva King Manifesting as a Youth.
The Gandharva King Subāhu, the Gandharva King Dharmarati,
and all such Gandharva kings gathered there in assembly.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of Kinnara kings.
These are the Kinnara King Wondrous Mouth, the Kinnara King Jewel Crown,
the Kinnara King Radiant Joy, the Kinnara King Delightful,
the Kinnara King Adorned with Wheels, and the Kinnara King Jewel Treasure.
The Kinnara King Mahodara, the Kinnara King Dṛḍhavīrya,
the Kinnara King Suvikrānta, the Kinnara King Śatamukha,
and the Kinnara King Mahāvṛkṣa.
All such kings of the kinnaras gathered there in assembly.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens,
namely the supreme celestial maiden and the celestial maiden Subhūṣitā.
The goddess Suvarṇamekhalā, the goddess Vibhūṣaṇā,
the goddess Śrutidharā, the goddess Amṛtacandrā,
the goddess Viśuddhakāyā, and the goddess Ratnaprabhā.
The goddess Puṣpakāyā, the goddess Devamukhī,
the goddess who utters the sounds of the five musical instruments from her mouth,
the goddess Sukhā, the goddess Suvarṇamālā, and the goddess Nīlotpalā.
The goddess Dharmasvaranirghoṣā, the goddess Sukhāvatī,
the goddess Sukhotpādā, the goddess Suviśuddhalakṣaṇā,
the goddess Suparigraha, and the goddess Dāna.
The celestial maiden Śuddhātmā,
as well as other such celestial maidens, also gathered there.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of daughters of the nāga kings.
They are the nāga girl named Mother of the Wondrously Adorned Holder, the nāga girl Ci-li-na,
the nāga girl Tri-jaṭī, the nāga girl Harmonious Countenance,
the nāga girl Victorious Auspiciousness, and the nāga girl Lightning Eye.
The nāga girl Vidyutprabhā, the nāga girl Citraśaila,
the hundred nāga girls of her retinue, the nāga girl Mahauṣadhi,
the nāga girl Candraprabhā, and the nāga girl Ekaśīrṣā.
The Nāga girl Hundred Arms, the Nāga girl Uprholder,
the Nāga girl Free from Affliction, the Nāga girl Well-Adorned,
the Nāga girl White Clouds, and the Nāga girl Car-Rider.
In the future, there will be the Dragon Girl of Many Retinues,
the Dragon Girl of the Ocean’s Womb, the Dragon Girl Who Veils Her Face,
the Dragon Girl of the Dharma Seat, and the Dragon Girl of the Wondrous Hand.
The Dragon Queen Sāgaragambhīrā, the Dragon Queen Meruśrī,
and all such dragon queens likewise gathered for the assembly.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of yakṣiṇīs.
They are the yakṣiṇī Priyamukhā, the yakṣiṇī Priyadattā,
the yakṣiṇī Adṛśyā, the yakṣiṇī Mañjuśrī, the yakṣiṇī Vajramālā, and the yakṣiṇī Sumālā.
The yakṣiṇī Vanalatā, the yakṣiṇī Puṣpavatī, the yakṣiṇī Kusumitā, the yakṣiṇī Ratnamālā,
the yakṣiṇī Manoramodarā, and the yakṣiṇī Śrīrājñī.
The gandharva maiden Drum-sound, the gandharva maiden Sublime Adornment,
the gandharva maiden Abundant Rites, the gandharva maiden Dharma-Love,
the gandharva maiden Dharma-Gift, and the gandharva maiden Blue Lotus.
The yakṣī Śatabāhu, the yakṣī Padmaśrī, the yakṣī Mahāpadmā, and the yakṣī Viśuddhakāyā.
The gandharva maiden Svairacāriṇī, the gandharva maiden Bhūmidā,
the gandharva maiden Phaladā, the gandharva maiden Siṃhagati,
the gandharva maiden Jvalanmāndārava, and the gandharva maiden Sumati.
The Gandharva maiden named Beneficent Bestower, the Gandharva maiden named Loving Patience,
the Gandharva maiden named Delighting in True Tranquility,
the Gandharva maiden named Jewel Sprout, and the Gandharva maiden named Delight of Śakra.
The yakṣī Lokendrasenā, the yakṣī Mṛgarājā, the yakṣī Nirmāṇalakṣmī, and the yakṣī Jvālāmukhī.
The yakṣiṇī who is liberated from greed, the yakṣiṇī who is liberated from hatred,
the yakṣiṇī who is liberated from delusion, and the yakṣiṇī who is a spiritual friend and a member of the retinue.
The Gandharva maiden Ratnasiṃhāsana, the Gandharva maiden Āgatāgatā,
the Gandharva maiden Jvālārciḥ, the Gandharva maiden Candraprabhā,
the Gandharva maiden Samantālokanetra, and the Gandharva maiden Suvarṇaprabhā.
The gandharva maiden Priyavatsā,
as well as these and other such gandharva maidens, also gathered for the assembly.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of kinnara maidens.
They are known as the Kinnarī One-Minded, the Kinnarī Profound-Minded,
the Wind-Walking Kinnarī, the Water-Walking Kinnarī,
the Sky-Traveling Kinnarī, and the Swift Kinnarī.
The Kinnarī Vastudā (Giver of Wealth), the Kinnarī Sundarakoṭi (Exquisite Tusk),
the Kinnarī Akṣobhyalakṣmī (Immovable Fortune), the Kinnarī Rañjanadhātu (Coloring Element),
the Kinnarī Jvalanaprabhāsamantā (Pervasive Blazing Light), and the Kinnarī Mañjuśrī (Mañjughoṣa).
The kinnarī Ratnapeṭā, the kinnarī Dravyadarśanā,
the kinnarī Sundarī, the kinnarī Vajramukhī, the kinnarī Suvarṇavarṇā, and the kinnarī Viśeṣavyūhā.
The Kinnarī Viśālānanā surrounded the Kinnarī Kalyāṇamitrā;
the Kinnarī Lokanāyikā and the Kinnarī Gaganarakṣitā.
The kinnarī Queen of Adornment, the kinnarī Jewel Topknot,
the kinnarī Total Retention Jewel, and the kinnarī Surrounded by the Wise.
The hundred *kiṃnara* maidens: the *Kiṃnara* maiden Bestower of Longevity,
the *Kiṃnara* maiden Upholder of the Buddha-Dharma, the *Kiṃnara* maiden Dharma-Realm Protector,
the *Kiṃnara* maiden Supreme Ornament, and the *Kiṃnara* maiden Supreme in an Instant.
One who seeks the Dharma always maintains the Kinnarī Vidyā;
such a person will constantly see Kinnarīs—the fearless Kinnarīs and the Kinnarīs who hasten toward liberation.
The Kinnarī Nityaguhyā, the Kinnarī Śīghradhāraṇī, the Kinnarī Kṣuraprabhājvālā, the Kinnarī Bhūmicārī,
the Kinnarī Devendrapālā, and the Kinnarī Surendrā.
The Kinnarī Jewel Queen, the Kinnarī of the Patience Division,
the Kinnarī Who Practices Giving, the Kinnarī of Many Abodes,
the Kinnarī Who Wields Weapons, and the Kinnarī of Sublime Adornments.
The Kinnarī Manojñā and other such Kinnarīs also came to the assembly.
Furthermore, hundreds of thousands of upāsakas and upāsikās also came to the assembly.
Furthermore, countless hundreds of thousands of others— both householders and renunciants,
as well as heterodox practitioners such as the Nirgranthas— also all came to that great assembly.
At that time, a great radiance issued forth from the Great Avīci Hell.
That light shone everywhere throughout the Jeta Grove,
and the entire garden was completely transformed into purity.
It manifests pillars adorned with celestial maṇi jewels,
subtle and perfectly complete;
it manifests great palatial towers embellished with gold and precious gems.
Furthermore, various chambers appeared: some were chambers of gold with doors of silver;
some were chambers of silver with doors of gold;
and some were chambers where gold and silver were interspersed.
The gates were fashioned with alternating bands of gold and silver.
There was a palace adorned with jewels, featuring alternating gold and silver,
and its pillars were made of exquisite jewels interspersed with gold and silver.
A golden palace appeared with pillars of white silver;
a white silver palace appeared with pillars of gold;
or a white silver palace was adorned with pillars made of various exquisite celestial jewels.
Upon the trees of the Jeta Grove,
there appeared various celestial and wondrous jewels as adornments;
furthermore, golden kalpa-trees appeared with leaves of white silver.
Upon those trees were various kinds of adornments;
they hung hundreds of varieties of exquisite garments, such as kauseya silk,
and were further draped with nets of precious jewels and hundreds of thousands of pearl necklaces.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of exquisite jeweled crowns, earrings,
and silk ribbons, adorned with intricate and various precious gems;
there were also exquisite miscellaneous flowers and exquisite bedding.
They were adorned with exquisite jeweled caskets.
Such variously adorned kalpavṛkṣa trees appeared in numbers reaching into the hundreds of thousands.
The gate-towers of the Jeta Grove’s various gardens had stairways made of exquisite vajra-jewels;
upon those towers were countless exquisite silk banners, pearls, and necklaces.
Adorned in this manner,
there were furthermore hundreds of thousands of exquisite jewel ponds,
filled with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.
Yet there were exquisite, perfect, and variegated flowers, namely: utpala flowers,
kumuda flowers, puṇḍarīka flowers, and māndārava flowers.
The pond was filled with *mahāmanāra* flowers, *udumbara* flowers, and others.
Furthermore, there were various kinds of exquisite flower trees,
namely *campaka* flower trees and *karavīra* flower trees.
There were *pāṭala* flower trees, exquisite *vimukti* flower trees,
fragrance-rain flower trees, and exquisite-intention flower trees;
there were such pleasing flower trees as these.
In that Jeta Grove, there appeared such rare and wondrous signs of pure and sublime adornment.
At that time, within the assembly was the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
Rising from his seat, he bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence,
gazed up at the Honored One’s countenance and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is rare, World-Honored One! There is now a matter of doubt within my mind that I wish to ask of the Tathāgata.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me leave to ask."
“World-Honored One, there is a great radiance here now.
From where does it come, and by what causes and conditions has such a rare and marvelous sign appeared?”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Good son, listen attentively;
I shall analyze and explain it for you."
This great radiance is the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
He has entered into the Great Avīci Hell for the purpose of delivering all sentient beings who are undergoing great suffering and affliction.
Having relieved them from their suffering, he entered the great city again to deliver all hungry ghosts (preta) from their misery.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin—
He addressed the Buddha again, saying,
"World-Honored One, that great Avīci Hell has iron walls surrounding it,
and its ground is likewise made of iron."
The perimeter of that city is continuous without interruption;
fierce fires with billowing smoke and flames burn perpetually.
Such is the nature of this evil realm within the hells.
There is a great cauldron of boiling water,
surging and bubbling, into which hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings are all cast.
It is like beans being boiled in a pot of water;
while they are boiling and bubbling, rising and falling,
they are cooked without interruption until they become soft and pulpy.
Sentient beings within the Avīci Hell undergo such suffering.
By what skillful means does the World-Honored One, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, enter therein?
The Blessed One again addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Son of good family, it is just as when a wheel-turning sage king enters the celestial garden of mani-jewels."
In this way, noble son,
when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara enters the Great Avīci Hell,
His body could not be obstructed by anything;
at that time, none of the various instruments of suffering in the Avīci Hell were able to oppress the Bodhisattva’s body.
The fierce fires of that great hell were completely extinguished, becoming a land of refreshing coolness.
At that time, Yama’s jailers within the hell were struck with alarm and doubt,
marveling at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Why is it that this place suddenly transforms into such a state of extreme suffering?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara enters the prison and shatters those cauldrons of boiling water, completely extinguishing the fierce fires.
That great pit of fire was transformed into a jewel pond,
within which lotuses were as large as chariot wheels.
At that time, the jailers of Yama saw this occurrence.
Taking various instruments of punishment— such as staves, bows, swords, hammers,
clubs, arrows, iron wheels, and tridents—
they went to the presence of the Devaputra Yama.
Having arrived, he said: "Great King, you are certainly able to know the ground of this karmic retribution of mine;
for what reason is it all completely extinguished?
Then the Devaputra Yama replied:
"How is it that the ground of the retribution for your karma has been entirely extinguished?
He further addressed the Devaputra Yama, saying,
"That great Avīci Hell has been transformed into a place of coolness."
At that time, there was a person of beautiful appearance,
adorned with a celestial, exquisite jeweled crown upon his topknot, who entered the hell.
The cauldron of boiling water was destroyed and the fire pit became a pond; within the pond, lotus flowers were as large as chariot wheels.
At that time, the Devaputra Yama reflected with focused thought:
"What celestial being possesses such majestic power?"
Is this the manifestation of Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, or others?
Upon reaching that hell, they manifest such inconceivable transformations;
could it be the majestic power and miraculous transformations of the mighty ten-headed Rākṣasa?
At that time, the Devaputra Yama,
using his supernormal power of the divine eye, surveyed this celestial realm;
having thus observed the various devas, he—
At that time, he further beheld Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva within the Avīci Hell.
Having seen him thus,
he quickly went to where Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at [the Buddha's] feet and,
uttering words of sincerity, praised him in verse:
"I take refuge in the Lotus King, Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion."
Maheśvara Śrī, who can grant the wishes of sentient beings and possesses great majestic power;
who subdues the most violent and evil realms of darkness as a bright lamp; and whom all who behold become fearless.
Manifesting a hundred thousand arms, his eyes are likewise so;
Complete with eleven faces, his wisdom is like the four great oceans;
Delighting in the subtle and wondrous Dharma, he acts to rescue all sentient beings.
Turtles, fish, and all aquatic beings— With supreme wisdom like a mountain,
he bestows jewels to relieve all living beings; Possessing supreme and greatest auspiciousness,
adorned with merit and wisdom, He enters even the Avīci Hell.
He transforms [the world] into a land of cool serenity;
all devas offer him worship and prostration as he bestows fearlessness.
He expounds the six pāramitās and constantly kindles the torch of the Dharma; his Dharma-eye is more brilliant than the sun.
With a majestic and wondrous physical form, his body like a mountain of gold;
with a sublime abdomen like the deep ocean of Dharma,
he is the true manifestation of the *cintāmaṇi* and the union of wondrous virtues within his mouth, having accumulated the various *samādhis*.
Countless hundreds of thousands of millions, possessing immeasurable happiness,
supreme in majesty, and most excellent sages— having attained liberation from the shackles within the terrifying evil realms, they bestow fearlessness upon all.
Surrounded by a multitude of followers, all their aspirations are fulfilled as if they had obtained a wish-fulfilling jewel; you destroy the city of the hungry ghosts,
opening it to the path of tranquility, and deliver the world from its maladies.
Like a parasol covering a banner, with the two nāgas Nanda and Upananda as armlets,
holding the *Amoghapāśa* (unfailing lasso) in hand and manifesting immeasurable majesty,
he is able to destroy the fears of the three realms.
The yakṣa Vajrapāṇi, the rākṣasas and bhūtas,
the piśācas and kumbhāṇḍas, and the apasmārakas— all of them are filled with terror.
With eyes like the *utpala* flower, the Sovereign Bestower of Fearlessness grants liberation from all various afflictions;
he enters hundreds of thousands of *samādhis*, as numerous as atoms.
He reveals all realms and causes all those within the evil destinies to attain liberation, thereby accomplishing the path to Bodhi.
At that time, the Devaputra Yama...
Having offered various praises and offerings to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
they circumambulated him three times and returned to their original places.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, will that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
having rescued those from suffering, return here to this assembly?
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Good son, after that Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara has emerged from the Great Avīci Hell,
he enters again the great city of the hungry ghosts."
Within it were countless hundreds of thousands of hungry ghosts whose mouths emitted flames,
their faces and eyes scorched, their bodies withered and emaciated,
their hair disheveled, and the hair on their bodies all bristling upright.
Their bellies are as vast as mountains, yet their throats are like needles.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara went to the great city of the hungry ghosts.
The blazing fires of karma within that city were all extinguished, transforming it into a state of coolness.
At that time, there was a gate-keeping demon general who held a red-hot iron staff;
he had a hideous form and a massive body, with two eyes deep crimson.
He gave rise to a mind of loving-kindness,
thinking, "I am now unable to protect such a land of evil karma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Arousing the mind of great compassion, rivers issued forth from each of his ten fingertips;
furthermore, rivers also issued from each of his toes,
and great rivers flowed from every single pore of his body.
These hungry ghosts drink the water therein;
while drinking this water, their throats become wide and their bodies become perfectly proportioned.
Furthermore, they obtain various kinds of food and drink of superior flavor, becoming entirely satiated.
Having obtained such benefit and peace and happiness,
these hungry ghosts each reflected deeply within their minds:
"For what reason do the people of Jambudvīpa [act as they do]?"
They constantly experience coolness, tranquility, and happiness.
Among them, some are well able to always practice reverence and filial support for their parents;
others are well able to practice generosity and follow virtuous friends.
There may be those who are wise, discerning, and always fond of the Mahāyāna;
there may be those who are well able to practice the Eightfold Noble Path;
and there may be those who are well able to strike the Dharma-gaṇḍī.
Some are well able to repair ruined monasteries;
some are well able to restore old Buddha-stūpas;
and some are well able to repair damaged *cakra* (wheel) finials of stūpas.
Some were well able to make offerings to and revere Dharma masters;
some were well able to see the places where the Tathāgatas walked in meditation;
and some were well able to see the places where the Bodhisattvas walked in meditation.
Some were well able to see the places where pratyekabuddhas had walked;
others were well able to see the places where arhats had walked.
They then reflected as follows:
In Jambudvīpa, there were such matters of spiritual practice as these.
At that time, from within this Mahāyāna-alaṃkāra-ratnarāja-sūtra,
a subtle and wondrous sound spontaneously issued forth.
When these hungry ghosts hear that sound,
the view of a self-body (satkāyadṛṣṭi) they cling to— though as high as a mountain peak— as well as all their afflictions,
are shattered without remainder by the vajra wisdom-mace.
They shall immediately attain rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss,
all becoming bodhisattvas named "Whosoever-Wishes-It-At-The-Mouth.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having rescued them from this suffering,
he then went to various other worlds to deliver sentient beings.
At that time, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Blessed One, has the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara come to this place to deliver sentient beings?
The Blessed One replied:
"Good son, this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara constantly and uninterruptedly delivers countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings;
he possesses great majestic power that exceeds even that of the Tathāgata."
Nivaraṇaviṣkambhin addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how is it that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such great majestic spiritual power?"
The Buddha told the son of good family: "In a past kalpa, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world,
named Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
At that time, I was the son of a certain elder named Wonderful Fragrant Mouth; there,
in the presence of that Buddha, I heard of these majestic and meritorious virtues of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Then Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding what I have heard concerning the majestic power and meritorious virtues of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, what are the details of these matters?"
The World-Honored One said,
"Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva brings forth the sun and moon from within his eyes."
From the center of the forehead emerges Maheśvara;
from the shoulders emerges Brahmā;
from the heart emerges Nārāyaṇa.
From his teeth emerged the Great Goddess of Eloquence;
from his mouth emerged the Wind Deity;
and from his navel emerged the Earth Deity.
The water-issuing Abdomen Deity.
From the body of Avalokiteśvara, such deities as these were born.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Great Lord (Maheśvara) Son of Heaven, saying:
"In the future, during the age of the final dharma,
within the realm of sentient beings..."
Yet there are sentient beings who cling to false views,
all of whom claim that you have been the Great Sovereign since beginningless time and are able to give birth to all sentient beings.
At that time, sentient beings, having lost the path to enlightenment and being deluded by ignorance, spoke thus:
"This great body of space takes the great earth as its seat;
both the objective world and sentient beings all emerge from this body."
"In this way, noble son,
after I had heard this from the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, another Buddha appeared."
He was named Śikhin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, at that time,
for the sake of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vīradatta,
I heard from that Buddha the majestic power and meritorious virtues of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin said:
"Bhagavān, what are the matters regarding the majestic spiritual power and meritorious virtues of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara as they have been heard by you?"
The Buddha said: "At that time, within the assembly of the Tathāgata Śikhin, all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans had gathered together."
At that time, when the World-Honored One was about to preach the Dharma within this assembly,
he emitted from his mouth various rays of light of diverse colors—

A bhikṣu should thus receive and maintain the three robes;
by doing so, one will attain the precepts, attain merit, and attain wisdom.
I say that bhikṣus should uphold this precept:
they must not misappropriate the property of the Saṃgha.
Such property is like a pit of fire; it is like poison.
Just as one who has taken heavy burdens or poison may still be cured,
those who misappropriate the property of the Sangha cannot be saved.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"I shall practice and train according to the Buddha’s instructions.
If a bhikṣu upholds the Prātimokṣa..."
"One should dwell well-established in guarding the training rules of the Blessed One.
Then the Venerable Ānanda prostrated at the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him, and withdrew.
Then the great śrāvakas each returned to their respective abodes.
All those in the world—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—did likewise.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
This concludes the fourth fascicle of the *Mahāyāna-alaṃkāra-ratnarāja-sūtra*.
